info.name: RestOpsIQ API
info.description:
Complete API test collection for RestOpsIQ.

Covers Health, Auth, MES Auth, MES Plant, Plant Production Orders (MES-05), Supply Items, and Testlab modules.

Global prefix: /api
Operational tenant (supply-items + MES + plant): {{tenantId}} = {{mesTenantId}} = palos-de-lena after seed.
TestLab: email auth only (no tenant).
MES plant: Bearer {{mesAccessToken}} (no x-tenant-id).
Supply-items: Bearer {{accessToken}} + x-tenant-id {{tenantId}}.

Phase completion is internal (no POST /api/plant/phases/complete). See postman/README.md.

// Skip if token is still valid
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ email, password }) }
// Treat token as valid for 14 minutes (access token TTL is 15 min)

// collection can be run multiple times against the same DB.
pm.test('Signup accepted (201) or user already exists (409)', () => {

item.name: Forgot Password
item.description:
RES-226 — Request a password reset email.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
Always returns 200 regardless of whether the email exists (anti-enumeration).
A BullMQ job is enqueued to send the email via Resend when the user exists.
The raw reset token is embedded in the email URL; extract it and set {{resetToken}} before running Reset Password.

exec: pm.test('Returns same message regardless of email existence (anti-enumeration)', () => {

item.name: Reset Password
item.description:
RES-226 — Reset the user's password using a valid single-use token.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
Prerequisite: run Forgot Password first, extract the raw token from the email link, and set {{resetToken}}.
Expected: 200 { message: 'Password updated successfully.' }
The token row in password_reset_tokens will have usedAt set after this call.

item.name: Reset Password — Invalid Token (negative)
item.description:
RES-226 negative case — attempt to reset password with a token that does not exist.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
Expected: 400 BadRequest with descriptive error message.

item.name: Reset Password — Reused Token (negative)
item.description:
RES-226 negative case — attempt to reuse a token that was already consumed by Reset Password.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
Prerequisite: run Reset Password successfully first ({{resetToken}} must be consumed).
Expected: 400 BadRequest 'Reset token has already been used'.

item.name: Resend Verification
item.description:
RES-226 — Resend the email verification OTP to an existing user.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
Always returns 200 regardless of whether the email exists (anti-enumeration).
A 6-digit OTP is stored in Redis under otp:{sha256(otpCode)} with a 15-minute TTL.
Extract the OTP from the email or Redis (redis-cli KEYS 'otp:*') and set {{otpCode}} before running Verify Email.

exec: pm.test('Returns same message regardless of email existence (anti-enumeration)', () => {

item.name: Verify Email
item.description:
RES-226 — Verify the user's email address using the 6-digit OTP.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
Prerequisite: run Resend Verification (or Signup which triggers sendVerifyEmail), then set {{otpCode}} from the email or Redis.
Expected: 200 { message: 'Email verified successfully.' }
The Redis key otp:{sha256(otpCode)} is deleted after successful verification.

item.name: Verify Email — Invalid OTP (negative)
item.description:
RES-226 negative case — attempt to verify email with a wrong 6-digit OTP.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
Expected: 400 BadRequest 'Invalid or expired verification code'.

item.name: MES Auth
item.description:
MES operational auth (cédula + PIN). Separate from TestLab email/password auth.

Prerequisites: Redis running, pnpm db:seed (see postman/README.md).
All login requests require header x-tenant-id: {{mesTenantId}}.
Protected requests use Bearer {{mesAccessToken}} (not {{accessToken}}).
Synthetic credentials are local/dev only — see apps/api/prisma/seed.ts header.

item.name: Login Owner
item.description:
POST /api/mes/auth/login with seeded OWNER credentials.
Requires x-tenant-id: {{mesTenantId}}.
Captures mesAccessToken, mesRefreshToken, and mesUserId (from JWT sub).

item.name: Me
item.description: GET /api/mes/auth/me — current operational user profile.

item.name: Get User Role
item.description:
GET /api/mes/users/:userId/role — OWNER role required.
Uses {{mesUserId}} from Login Owner or Me.

item.name: Create User
item.description:
POST /api/mes/users — OWNER role required.
Creates an OPERATOR with a unique synthetic cédula (pre-request script).
Requires Bearer {{mesAccessToken}} from Login Owner.
Captures mesCreatedUserId on success.

item.name: Logout
item.description: POST /api/mes/auth/logout — clears refresh token and blacklists JWT jti when present.

item.name: Login — Wrong PIN (negative)
item.description: Negative case — invalid PIN returns generic 401.

item.name: Login — Missing x-tenant-id (negative)
item.description: Negative case — login without x-tenant-id header returns 400.

item.name: MES Plant
item.description:
MES plant master data (workstations, recipes, phases, inputs).

Prerequisites: run **MES Auth → Login Owner** first (sets {{mesAccessToken}}).

Auth: Bearer {{mesAccessToken}} only — do **not** send x-tenant-id (tenant comes from JWT, palos-de-lena).

Run in folder order. Use {{supplyItemId}} from seed or **02 Supply Items → Create** (same operational tenant as MES).

item.name: Create Work Station
item.description: POST /api/plant/workstations — unique code per run.

item.name: Create Recipe (nested)
item.description: POST /api/plant/recipes — 2 phases, no inputs (supply is tenant-scoped).

item.name: Get Recipe Detail
item.description: GET detail — captures phaseId1/phaseId2 and asserts totalStandardMinutes.

item.name: Reorder Phases
item.description: PATCH reorder — body is a JSON array [{ phaseId, newOrder }].

item.name: Add Phase Input — invalid supply (negative)
item.description: POST with unknown supplyItemId — expect 404 (tenant from MES JWT).

item.name: Add Phase Input
item.description: Happy path — uses {{supplyItemId}} (seeded or from 02 Supply Items → Create). Must belong to operational tenant palos-de-lena.

exec: // Accept 201 or 404 when supplyItemId is from another tenant

item.name: Delete Phase Input
item.description: Runs after Add Phase Input when 201; may 404 if prior step failed.

item.name: Soft Delete Work Station
item.description: Soft delete — blocked with 409 if active phase executions exist on station.

item.name: Plant — Production Orders
item.description:
MES-05 production order lifecycle + QA approve.

Prerequisites: **MES Auth → Login Owner** (sets {{mesAccessToken}}).

Run this folder top-to-bottom. Setup creates a 5-phase recipe (phase 2 requires QA).

**No** `POST /api/plant/phases/complete` — chain completion is internal (`PhaseChainService`). Use unit tests or a dev script before **QA Approve Execution**.

Pause/resume require order status `IN_PROCESS` (operator runtime — not in MES-05 HTTP); those requests accept 200 or 409.

item.name: Setup — Create Work Station (Orders)
item.description: Creates a workstation for the 5-phase orders recipe.

item.name: Setup — Create 5-Phase Recipe (Orders)
item.description: 5 phases; phase 2 has requiresQA=true for QA approve smoke.

item.name: Create Production Order
item.description: POST /api/plant/orders — creates OP + 5 PENDING executions.

exec: const qaExec = body.executions.find((ex) => ex.requiresQA === true) || body.executions[0];

item.name: List Production Orders
item.description: GET /api/plant/orders

item.name: Get Production Order Detail
item.description: GET /api/plant/orders/:id

item.name: Plan Production Order
item.description: PATCH /api/plant/orders/:id/plan — first phase → READY.

item.name: Pause Production Order
item.description: POST /api/plant/orders/:id/pause — requires order IN_PROCESS (409 if still PLANNED).

item.name: Resume Production Order
item.description: POST /api/plant/orders/:id/resume — requires order PAUSED.

item.name: QA Approve Execution
item.description: POST /api/plant/executions/:id/qa-approve — run after internal completeExecution + COMPLETED QA phase (see README).

exec: pm.test('Status 200 or expected client error', () => pm.expect([200, 400, 404, 409]).to.include(code));

item.name: Cancel Production Order
item.description: POST /api/plant/orders/:id/cancel — after plan (PLANNED) reason only; add consumedInputsAction when IN_PROCESS/PAUSED.

item.name: 02 Supply Items
item.description:
All requests require x-tenant-id: {{tenantId}} header.
Run order matters: Create first (captures supplyItemId), Delete last.

Testlab requests must run top-to-bottom: Projects → Milestones → Requirements → Suites → Cases → Runs.
Each POST create captures an ID used by subsequent requests in the same sub-folder.
